title: Micah Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Micah chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Micah Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Micah Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Micah 7:1, what is the speaker compared to?
options: Gathered summer fruits and the grapegleanings of the vintage
questions.correctAnswer: Gathered summer fruits and the grapegleanings of the vintage
questions.explanation: Micah 7:1 compares the speaker to when they have gathered the summer fruits and the grapegleanings of the vintage, indicating scarcity.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:2, what has perished out of the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: The good man
questions.explanation: Micah 7:2 states that the good man is perished out of the earth and there is none upright among men.

questions.question: In Micah 7:3, what do the prince and judge ask for?
questions.correctAnswer: A reward
questions.explanation: Micah 7:3 says the prince asketh, and the judge asketh for a reward.

questions.question: Micah 7:4 compares the best and most upright people to what?
questions.correctAnswer: Briers and a thorn hedge
questions.explanation: Micah 7:4 describes the best as a brier and the most upright as sharper than a thorn hedge.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:5, whom should you not trust?
questions.correctAnswer: A friend and a guide
questions.explanation: Micah 7:5 advises not to trust in a friend or put confidence in a guide.

questions.question: Who does Micah 7:6 say are a man's enemies?
options: The men of his own house
questions.correctAnswer: The men of his own house
questions.explanation: Micah 7:6 states that a man's enemies are the men of his own house, such as son against father and daughter against mother.

questions.question: In Micah 7:7, to whom will the speaker look and wait?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Micah 7:7 says the speaker will look unto the LORD and wait for the God of salvation.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 7:2 states that there are many upright men on the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 7:2 declares that there is none upright among men, meaning no upright men exist at that time.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 7:6 says that family members will act as enemies to one another.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 7:6 clearly states that a man's enemies are the men of his own house, with family members dishonoring each other.

questions.question: True or False: According to Micah 7:5, you should trust in a guide.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 7:5 instructs not to put confidence in a guide.

questions.question: True or False: In Micah 7:7, the speaker expresses confidence that God will hear him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 7:7 says the speaker will wait for the God of salvation and that God will hear him.

questions.question: Which action comes first in Micah 7:1-7?
options: The speaker compares himself to gathered summer fruits
The speaker trusts in the LORD
The speaker warns not to trust friends
The speaker describes family members as enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The speaker compares himself to gathered summer fruits
questions.explanation: The comparison to gathered summer fruits occurs in Micah 7:1, which comes before the other actions in verses 5-7.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:3, what do the great men express?
questions.correctAnswer: Mischievous desire
questions.explanation: Micah 7:3 states that the great man uttereth his mischievous desire.

questions.question: In Micah 7:4, what will come upon the watchmen and visitation?
questions.correctAnswer: Perplexity
questions.explanation: Micah 7:4 says the day of the watchmen and visitation cometh, and now shall be their perplexity.

questions.question: In Micah 7:1, what fruit does the speaker desire?
questions.correctAnswer: Firstripe fruit
questions.explanation: Micah 7:1 ends with the speaker's soul desiring the firstripe fruit.

medium.title: Micah Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Micah Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:8, what will the LORD be when the speaker sits in darkness?
questions.correctAnswer: A light unto me
questions.explanation: Micah 7:8 explicitly states, 'when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me,' indicating God's guiding presence in times of trouble.

questions.question: In Micah 7:9, why does the speaker say he will bear the indignation of the LORD?
options: Because I have sinned against Him
Because I have helped the poor
Because I have trusted in man
Because I have been faithful in prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Because I have sinned against Him
questions.explanation: Micah 7:9 states, 'I will bear the indignation of the LORD, because I have sinned against him,' showing the speaker's acknowledgment of personal sin and God's discipline.

questions.question: What does Micah 7:10 say will happen to the enemy who mocked the LORD's presence?
options: She shall be trodden down as the mire of the streets
She shall be exalted among the nations
She shall find refuge in the wilderness
She shall be forgiven and restored
questions.correctAnswer: She shall be trodden down as the mire of the streets
questions.explanation: Micah 7:10 describes that the enemy who questioned 'Where is the LORD thy God?' will face shame and be 'trodden down as the mire of the streets,' indicating judgment and humiliation.

questions.question: True or False: According to Micah 7:11, when the walls are rebuilt, the decree will be far removed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 7:11 states, 'In the day that thy walls are to be built, in that day shall the decree be far removed,' indicating a time of restoration when judgment is taken away.

questions.question: From where does Micah 7:12 say people will come in the day of restoration?
options: From the desert and the mountains
From the east and the west
questions.correctAnswer: From Assyria and fortified cities
questions.explanation: Micah 7:12 says, 'he shall come even to thee from Assyria, and from the fortified cities...,' showing a gathering of people from distant lands in the day of blessing.

questions.question: How does Micah 7:13 describe the land despite the coming restoration?
options: The land shall be desolate because of the inhabitants
The land shall flourish with abundance
The land shall be filled with peace and joy
The land shall be restored to its former glory
questions.correctAnswer: The land shall be desolate because of the inhabitants
questions.explanation: Micah 7:13 states, 'Notwithstanding the land shall be desolate because of them that dwell therein, for the fruit of their doings,' showing consequences of the people's actions despite restoration promises.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:14, where does God instruct to feed His people?
options: In Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old
questions.correctAnswer: In Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old
questions.explanation: Micah 7:14 commands feeding the flock in Bashan and Gilead 'as in the days of old,' indicating a return to past blessings and provision.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is emphasized in Micah 7:7 about how the speaker responds to adversity?
options: Faith and patience in the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and patience in the LORD
questions.explanation: Micah 7:7 says, 'Therefore I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation,' highlighting faith and patient trust in God during difficulties.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 7:16 teaches that the nations will be empowered and confident before God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 7:16 says the nations 'shall be confounded at all their might: they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf,' showing fear and shame, not confidence.

questions.question: What does Micah 7:18 say God delights in?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Micah 7:18 states that God 'retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy,' emphasizing God's loving and forgiving nature.

questions.question: How does Micah 7:19 describe God’s treatment of our sins?
options: He casts all their sins into the depths of the sea
He hides them in the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: He casts all their sins into the depths of the sea
questions.explanation: Micah 7:19 says God 'will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea,' illustrating complete forgiveness.

questions.question: What promise in Micah 7:15 connects to the deliverance from Egypt?
options: God will show marvelous things as in the days of Egypt
God will never deliver His people again
God will punish Egypt for their sins
God will lead a new exodus through Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: God will show marvelous things as in the days of Egypt
questions.explanation: Micah 7:15 connects God's future works to His mighty acts during the Exodus, promising similar marvelous deeds.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:17, what will the nations do because of the LORD our God and His people?
options: They shall be afraid and fear
They shall rise up in rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be afraid and fear
questions.explanation: Micah 7:17 states the nations 'shall be afraid of the LORD our God, and shall fear because of thee,' showing respect and reverence for God's power.

questions.question: What does Micah 7:6 warn about trusting close relationships?
options: A man's enemies are the men of his own house
The family is a source of unity
questions.correctAnswer: A man's enemies are the men of his own house
questions.explanation: Micah 7:6 warns that even close family members can become enemies, highlighting caution in trusting relationships.

questions.question: True or False: According to Micah 7:20, God has sworn mercy to Abraham and will perform this truth to Jacob.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 7:20 confirms God's faithfulness to His promises by stating He will 'perform the truth to Jacob, and the mercy to Abraham, which thou hast sworn unto our fathers.'

hard.title: Micah Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Micah Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:15, the marvelous things shown to the people will be according to the days of what significant event?
options: The days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt
The days of thy captivity in Babylon
The days of the judges in Israel
The days of the temple's destruction
questions.correctAnswer: The days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: Micah 7:15 explicitly states that marvelous things will be shown according to the days of the coming out of Egypt, referencing the Exodus event which is foundational for Israel's identity.

questions.question: What reaction do the nations have when they see the mighty acts of God mentioned in Micah 7:16?
options: They shall be confounded and lay their hand upon their mouth
They shall celebrate and praise the LORD
They shall wage war against Israel
They shall ignore and remain silent
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be confounded and lay their hand upon their mouth
questions.explanation: Micah 7:16 describes the nations' reaction as one of confusion and silence, laying their hand upon their mouth and their ears becoming deaf, indicating shock and awe at God's power.

questions.question: In Micah 7:17, the nations are compared to which creatures to illustrate their fear and humiliation before God?
questions.correctAnswer: Serpents and worms
questions.explanation: Micah 7:17 uses the imagery of serpents licking the dust and worms moving out of their holes to depict the humbled and fearful state of the nations before the LORD.

questions.question: Micah 7:18 praises God for what unique attribute that shows His mercy toward His people?
options: That pardoneth iniquity and passeth by the transgression
That performs miracles and signs without end
That commands the armies of heaven
That judges all people without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: That pardoneth iniquity and passeth by the transgression
questions.explanation: Micah 7:18 highlights God's mercy in pardoning iniquity and passing over transgressions, emphasizing His unique compassion toward His remnant people.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:19, what does God do with the sins of His people?
options: Casts all their sins into the depths of the sea
Transfers their sins to a scapegoat
questions.correctAnswer: Casts all their sins into the depths of the sea
questions.explanation: Micah 7:19 declares that God casts all sins into the depths of the sea, symbolizing complete forgiveness and removal of guilt.

questions.question: Micah 7:20 affirms God's covenant faithfulness to which two patriarchs?
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob and Abraham
questions.explanation: Micah 7:20 mentions God's promises to Jacob and Abraham, affirming the covenantal mercy and truth that God has sworn to the patriarchs from ancient times.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God casting sins into the depths of the sea, as stated in Micah 7:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 103:12
questions.explanation: Psalm 103:12 similarly speaks of God removing sins far from us, as far as the east is from the west, paralleling Micah's imagery of casting sins into the sea.

questions.question: In Micah 7:15, the phrase 'marvellous things' can be understood as a foreshadowing of which New Testament event?
options: The coming of Jesus Christ as the Savior
The building of the second temple
questions.correctAnswer: The coming of Jesus Christ as the Savior
questions.explanation: The 'marvellous things' shown according to the Exodus days foreshadow God's ultimate salvation through Jesus Christ, who fulfills the deliverance themes.

questions.question: The literary device used in Micah 7:18, where contrasting ideas of God's anger and mercy are presented, is best described as what?
questions.correctAnswer: Paradox
questions.explanation: Micah 7:18 presents a paradox by showing God as one who retains not His anger forever because He delights in mercy, combining seemingly opposite traits.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'pardoneth' in Micah 7:18, and what does it imply about God's nature?
options: 'Nasa' meaning to lift or bear, implying God removes the burden of sin
'Chesed' meaning lovingkindness, implying God's covenant love
questions.correctAnswer: 'Nasa' meaning to lift or bear, implying God removes the burden of sin
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'nasa' means to lift or bear, used here to indicate God lifts away or pardons iniquity, highlighting His forgiving nature as in Micah 7:18.

questions.question: Micah 7:16 describes the nations as laying their hand upon their mouth and having deaf ears. What does this imagery signify in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: Shock and silence in face of God's overwhelming power
questions.correctAnswer: Shock and silence in face of God's overwhelming power
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, covering the mouth and deafness symbolize astonishment and inability to respond, indicating the nations' helplessness before God's acts as per Micah 7:16.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s mercy and forgiveness like that found in Micah 7:18-19?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 2:4-5
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:4-5 emphasizes God’s rich mercy and love, made alive us in Christ despite our sins, echoing Micah’s themes of pardon and compassion.

questions.question: Micah 7:17’s imagery of nations licking dust and moving out of holes is an example of which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: The use of 'like a serpent' and 'like worms' are similes comparing the humbled nations to lowly creatures, vividly illustrating their fear as in Micah 7:17.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 7:20 confirms that God's mercy and truth are promises newly given to Israel and not related to past covenants.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 7:20 states that the mercy and truth are those which God has sworn unto the fathers from the days of old, linking them to ancient covenants, not new promises.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 7:19 affirms that God will subdue the iniquities of His people and cast their sins into the depths of the sea.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 7:19 explicitly states that God will have compassion, subdue iniquities, and cast all sins into the depths of the sea, affirming His forgiveness.

theological.title: Micah Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Micah Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:2, what describes the moral state of humanity?
options: The good man is perished and none is upright; all lie in wait for blood
All men are righteous and upright before God
Humanity is mostly compassionate and forgiving
Most people seek peace and justice
questions.correctAnswer: The good man is perished and none is upright; all lie in wait for blood
questions.explanation: Micah 7:2 states that 'The good man is perished out of the earth: and there is none upright among men: they all lie in wait for blood; they hunt every man his brother with a net,' highlighting the depravity and corruption of humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated in Micah 7:18 when it says God 'pardoneth iniquity and delighteth in mercy'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and forgiveness
questions.explanation: Micah 7:18 emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness as He pardons iniquity and passes by transgressions, demonstrating His gracious and merciful nature.

questions.question: What theological truth is taught by Micah 7:19 regarding sin and God's response?
options: God subdues our iniquities and casts all sins into the depths of the sea
God removes sin but keeps a record of it
questions.correctAnswer: God subdues our iniquities and casts all sins into the depths of the sea
questions.explanation: Micah 7:19 teaches that God will ‘subdue our iniquities’ and ‘cast all their sins into the depths of the sea,’ illustrating the doctrine of divine forgiveness and cleansing from sin.

questions.question: How does Micah 7:7 express a correct posture of faith amidst human failure?
options: By looking unto the LORD and waiting for the God of salvation
By trusting in human friends and guides
By relying on one's own righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: By looking unto the LORD and waiting for the God of salvation
questions.explanation: Micah 7:7 declares the believer's trust and patient waiting on God, demonstrating faith in God's salvation despite human corruption.

questions.question: According to Micah 7:3, what corrupt behaviors do the leaders exhibit?
options: Princes and judges ask for bribes and great men utter mischievous desires
questions.correctAnswer: Princes and judges ask for bribes and great men utter mischievous desires
questions.explanation: Micah 7:3 reveals that leaders are corrupt, seeking bribes and uttering evil desires, which corrupts the administration of justice.

questions.question: What does the comparison in Micah 7:4 between the best and a brier signify about human nature?
options: Even the best people are harmful and painful like a brier or thorn hedge
The best people are gentle and kind
The best are like fruitful vineyards
questions.correctAnswer: Even the best people are harmful and painful like a brier or thorn hedge
questions.explanation: Micah 7:4 compares even the best humans to briers and thorns, emphasizing the pervasive moral corruption and danger in human nature.

questions.question: What does the prophetic promise in Micah 7:15 reveal about God's salvific acts?
options: God will show marvelous things as in the days of the Exodus from Egypt
God will abandon His people without intervention
Salvation depends solely on human effort
God will punish Israel without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God will show marvelous things as in the days of the Exodus from Egypt
questions.explanation: Micah 7:15 recalls the Exodus, emphasizing God's power to deliver and perform miraculous salvation, illustrating continuity in God's redemptive work.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching emerges from Micah 7:18 and Micah 7:19 about God's character and sin?
options: God is merciful and forgives sin by subduing iniquity and casting sins into the sea
God is indifferent to human sinfulness
God punishes sin eternally without remission
God's wrath never ceases and is not balanced by mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God is merciful and forgives sin by subduing iniquity and casting sins into the sea
questions.explanation: Micah 7:18-19 together reveal that God delights in mercy, pardons iniquity, and completely removes sin, showing a profound divine forgiveness.

questions.question: What insight about social relationships and trust is taught by synthesizing Micah 7:5-6 with Micah 7:11?
options: Human relationships are broken and untrustworthy, but God’s restoration will bring stability
One should trust friends and guides for security
Family bonds are unbreakable and secure
Social order is permanent without divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: Human relationships are broken and untrustworthy, but God’s restoration will bring stability
questions.explanation: Micah 7:5-6 shows broken trust even within families, while 7:11 promises restored walls and security, teaching that human failure necessitates divine restoration.

questions.question: How does Micah 7:12-13 contribute to the narrative arc of Israel’s judgment and restoration?
options: Foreign nations will come to Israel, but the land remains desolate due to sin
Israel will be completely destroyed with no hope
Israel conquers all nations without judgment
The land flourishes without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: Foreign nations will come to Israel, but the land remains desolate due to sin
questions.explanation: Micah 7:12-13 depicts an invasion by foreign powers juxtaposed with desolation caused by Israel’s sin, highlighting judgment within the redemptive history.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Micah 7:8-10 provide against the claim that God is absent in times of suffering?
options: God is present as a light in darkness and will vindicate the righteous
God abandons the suffering and is silent
Enemies triumph permanently over the faithful
questions.correctAnswer: God is present as a light in darkness and will vindicate the righteous
questions.explanation: Micah 7:8-10 affirms that even in suffering and darkness, God is a light and will bring justice, countering sceptical claims of divine absence.

questions.question: What does Micah 7:17 teach about the fear of God in relation to nations and individuals?
options: Nations and individuals will fear the LORD because of His power manifested through His people
Fear of God is irrelevant to nations
God's power causes nations to worship idols
Nations are victorious over God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: Nations and individuals will fear the LORD because of His power manifested through His people
questions.explanation: Micah 7:17 describes nations being afraid of God and fearing because of His people, showing God's sovereignty over all creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly highlighted in Micah 7:20 where God is said to perform 'truth to Jacob' and 'mercy to Abraham'?
options: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises
God's impartiality to all nations equally
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Micah 7:20 emphasizes God's faithfulness in fulfilling His covenantal promises made to the patriarchs, highlighting His steadfast love and truth.

questions.question: What theological insight arises from combining Micah 7:1 and Micah 7:2 about the human condition?
options: Humanity is spiritually barren and morally corrupt, lacking good and upright people
Humanity is spiritually fruitful and morally upright
All people are trustworthy and just
Humanity naturally desires only good fruit
questions.correctAnswer: Humanity is spiritually barren and morally corrupt, lacking good and upright people
questions.explanation: Micah 7:1-2 together depict a barren spiritual condition and pervasive moral corruption, with no good or upright person left on earth.

questions.question: How does Micah 7:14 illustrate God's role as shepherd in the context of His people’s restoration?
options: God feeds and leads His people like a shepherd with His rod
God abandons His people to their own devices
God leaves His people scattered and unguided
God ignores the plight of His heritage
questions.correctAnswer: God feeds and leads His people like a shepherd with His rod
questions.explanation: Micah 7:14 depicts God as a shepherd who feeds and guides His flock, symbolizing His care and leadership in restoring His people.
